title: AgentEvalSuite
description: RFC 0081 §A. A portable, host-agnostic evaluation suite for a manifest agent (RFC 0003/0070): the tasks, the expected outputs or rubrics, the deterministic tool/memory fixtures, the allowed model classes, and the pass/fail thresholds that answer "is this agent good enough to deploy?". Distributed inside a pack tarball and referenced by URI exactly like `systemPromptRef` / `handoff.*SchemaRef` (RFC 0003 §C/§D) — NOT embedded in `AgentManifest`. A host advertising `agents.evalSuite` executes a suite as an eval run (a `mode: "eval"` projection over `POST /runs`, RFC 0081 §B) and terminates with an `eval-summary.schema.json` scorecard. The suite carries NO secret material and NO host-internal identifiers (it is authored offline and shipped in a signed pack).

suiteId.description: Globally unique suite identifier in the `<scope>.<org>.evals.<name>` convention (e.g. `core.openwop.evals.support-resolver`), mirroring the pack `<scope>.<author>.<pack>` namespace (RFC 0003). The `.evals.` infix distinguishes a suite from an agent/pack id.

version.description: SemVer of the suite. A suite version is pinned on an eval run (carried on `eval.started.suiteVersion` and `eval-summary.suiteVersion`) so a regression comparison (§D `regression` mode) is between like versions.

targetAgentId.description: MAY. The `AgentManifest.id` this suite is authored for. Absent ⇒ the suite is agent-agnostic and MAY be pointed at any `agentId` at run time (the run request carries the `agentId`). When present, a host SHOULD reject an eval run whose target `agentId` differs, unless the caller explicitly overrides.

modes.description: The eval modes this suite exercises (RFC 0081 §D closed vocabulary). `golden`: exact / contains / json-match against each task's `expected`. `rubric`: a host-chosen judge scores against weighted criteria (nondeterministic — a recorded-fact score). `adversarial`: tasks probe for unsafe / jailbreak behavior; `safetyFindings` is the primary output. `regression`: re-run against a new agent/model/prompt version and diff scores vs a `baselineRunId` (composes RFC 0054 `:diff`). `live-shadow`: run against LIVE tools/memory instead of `fixtures` — the only mode that bypasses fixture injection; explicitly nondeterministic. A run MUST request only modes the suite declares here AND the host advertises (`capabilities.agents.evalSuite.modes`); an unadvertised mode is rejected at run-create with `400 validation_error`.

allowedModels.description: MAY. The `AgentManifest.modelClass` values (RFC 0002) the suite is valid for. Absent ⇒ valid for any class. A host SHOULD record the `evaluatedModelClass` on the summary so a score is interpreted against the model it was produced with.

thresholds.description: MAY. The pass/fail bar for the suite. A task or the aggregate `passed` flag is computed against these. Absent ⇒ the host's default bar (the summary still carries raw scores).

passScore.description: The minimum aggregate score (0.0–1.0) for `EvalSummary.passed: true`.

maxCostUsd.description: MAY. The maximum total cost (summed from RFC 0026 `provider.usage`) for a passing run. A run that exceeds it MUST NOT report `passed: true` even if `passScore` is met.

maxP95LatencyMs.description: MAY. The maximum p95 per-task latency for a passing run.

trials.description: RFC 0244 §B. MAY. Repeated trials. A host MUST run each task `count` times, each as its own child agent invocation started from the same fixtures and `memorySeed` snapshot; memory one trial writes MUST NOT be visible to another trial of the run, and a fixture cursor resets per trial. `k` MUST NOT exceed `count` (a suite rule, not a schema conditional). `count` > 1 requires `agents.evalSuite.trials` with `count` <= `maxTrials`, else the suite is refused at run-create with `400 validation_error`. Cost ceilings count every trial.

k.description: The k of pass@k and pass^k. Absent: `count`.

passRule.description: A task passes when: `all`, every trial passed; `any`, at least one did; `mean`, the mean trial score >= `thresholds.passScore`.

tasks.description: The eval tasks. Each is executed as one child agent invocation (the RFC 0077 `agent.invocation.*` bracket + the existing `agent.*` / `provider.usage` events), scored, and reported via a per-task `eval.scored` event + an `EvalSummary` entry.

taskId.description: Suite-unique task identifier (kebab-case). Carried verbatim on `eval.scored.taskId` and the per-task summary entry.

input.description: The run input for the task, validated against the agent's input schema by the host. An opaque object/value — content is task-defined.

expected.description: How the task is scored. `golden`: deterministic match against `match`. `rubric`: a judge scores against weighted `rubric` criteria.

kind.description: Scoring mode for this task. A suite declaring a non-`golden`/`rubric` `modes` entry (e.g. `adversarial`) still scores each task via one of these two `kind`s. `trajectory` (RFC 0244 §A): the task is graded on its tool path alone; its score is 1 when `trajectory` matched and 0 otherwise, and it carries `trajectory` and neither `match` nor `rubric` (a suite rule, not a schema conditional: COMPATIBILITY.md §2.4).

strategy.description: `exact`: stringified output equals `value`. `contains`: output contains `value`. `json-match`: output JSON-deep-equals `value` (key order / whitespace insensitive).

value.description: The expected value for the strategy. Opaque.

rubric.description: Present when `kind: "rubric"`. Weighted criteria a judge scores the output against; the task score is the weighted sum of met criteria, normalized to 0.0–1.0. Judge selection + scoring is host-internal (nondeterministic — the score is a recorded fact).

criterion.description: A human-readable scoring criterion (e.g. "cites the 30-day refund window").

weight.description: Relative weight of this criterion (criteria weights SHOULD sum to 1.0 across the task).

trajectory.description: RFC 0244 §A. MAY. The tool path the task is held to, graded from the `agent.tool-called` events in each trial's `agent.invocation-*` bracket whose `agentId` is the task's target agent (every call in the bracket when `includeDelegates` is true). On a `golden` or `rubric` task a trial MUST NOT pass unless the trajectory matched, and its score stays the output score. Requires `agents.evalSuite.trajectory`; a host that does not advertise it MUST refuse the suite at run-create with `400 validation_error`.

match.description: `exact`: same length, and the i-th observed call matches the i-th expected call. `in-order`: the expected calls match a subsequence of the observed calls, in order; extra calls allowed. `any-order`: each expected call matches a distinct observed call, any order; extra calls allowed. `subset`: every observed call matches some expected call; no tool outside `calls` was called.

args.description: MAY. The expected arguments, compared under `argsMatch`. Suite content: never echoed onto the wire.

argsMatch.description: RFC 0244 §A. How `args` is compared with the call's `inputs`. `ignore` (default): not compared. `exact`: `inputs` JSON-deep-equals `args`. `subset`: every key path in `args` is present in `inputs` with a JSON-deep-equal value. The host compares the call as executed, before any wire redaction.

calls.description: The expected calls, in order where the mode reads order.

forbidden.description: MAY. Tools that MUST NOT be called. One call to any of them makes the trajectory unmatched, whatever the mode.

includeDelegates.description: MAY. `true` grades every `agent.tool-called` in the bracket, delegates and fan-out children included, in log order. Default: the target agent's own calls only.

fixtures.description: MAY. Deterministic substitutes for live tool/memory I/O so a `golden`/`regression` eval is reproducible. When present, the eval host MUST inject `toolResponses` in place of live tool calls and seed `memorySeed` before the invocation. The `live-shadow` mode is the explicit exception — it ignores `fixtures` and runs against live tools/memory.

toolResponses.description: Canned tool results keyed by tool invocation, injected in place of live tool calls. RFC 0244 §D: each call is served the first unconsumed entry whose `tool` and `args` match; an entry is consumed once, so repeated calls walk a scripted sequence.

tool.description: The `<scope>:<tool-id>` (RFC 0077 `toolAllowlist` / RFC 0078) the response stands in for.

response.description: The canned result the host returns for that tool. Opaque.

args.description: RFC 0244 §D. MAY. The arguments this response answers, compared under `argsMatch`. Absent with `argsMatch` absent: the entry answers any call to `tool`.

argsMatch.description: RFC 0244 §A. How `args` is compared with the call's `inputs`. `ignore` (default): not compared. `exact`: `inputs` JSON-deep-equals `args`. `subset`: every key path in `args` is present in `inputs` with a JSON-deep-equal value. The host compares the call as executed, before any wire redaction.

memorySeed.description: Memory entries seeded into the agent's read snapshot before the invocation (RFC 0004 `MemoryAdapter` shape). Tenant-scoped + SR-1-redacted on the host side exactly like any memory write.

onMiss.description: RFC 0244 §D. MAY. `fail`: a call matching no unconsumed entry MUST NOT reach a live tool or any external side effect; the host returns a tool error to the agent, counts it in the task's `fixtureMissCount`, and reports the trial `passed: false` and `score: 0`. `live`: a miss MAY call the live tool, and the task's `fixtureMissCount` MUST then be > 0. Absent: the RFC 0081 behaviour is unchanged (a host SHOULD treat it as `fail`). Requires `agents.evalSuite.fixtureMatching`, as does `toolResponses[].args`.
